title: Max Temperature
statement:
You are given an array of daily temperatures (integers, may be negative). Return the highest temperature. If the array is empty, return null.

Example: [3, -2, 9, 4] -> 9
Example: [] -> null
Constraints: 0 <= length <= 10^5

answerKey.pattern: Single linear scan keeping a running maximum
keyPoints: Start the running max from the first element (or -Infinity)
Visit every element once and update the max when the current value is larger
Return the max at the end
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Sort and take the last element: O(n log n)

title: Second Largest Score
statement:
Given an array of integer scores, return the second largest DISTINCT score. If there are fewer than two distinct scores, return null.

Example: [4, 9, 7] -> 7
Example: [5, 5, 3] -> 3
Example: [8, 8] -> null
Constraints: 0 <= length <= 10^5

answerKey.pattern: Single pass tracking the largest and second largest distinct values
keyPoints: Keep two variables: first and second (start at -Infinity or null)
If x > first: second = first, first = x
Else if x < first and x > second: second = x (x must be strictly smaller than first so duplicates of the max are skipped)
Return null if second was never set
edgeCases: Fewer than two distinct values returns null
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Deduplicate with a Set and sort: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

title: Duplicate Badge
statement:
A door scanner logs badge IDs as an array of integers. Return true if any badge ID appears more than once, otherwise false.

Example: [4, 7, 1, 7] -> true
Example: [3, 9, 2] -> false
Constraints: 0 <= length <= 10^5

answerKey.pattern: Hash set to remember IDs already seen
keyPoints: Create an empty set
For each ID: if it is already in the set return true, otherwise add it
Return false after the loop
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Nested loops comparing every pair: O(n^2) time, O(1) space
Sort then compare neighbours: O(n log n)

title: Two Tickets
statement:
You are given an array of ticket prices and a budget. Return the indices [i, j] (i < j) of the two tickets whose prices add up exactly to the budget. Exactly one valid pair exists, and you may not use the same ticket twice.

Example: prices = [12, 5, 9, 20], budget = 14 -> [1, 2]
Example: prices = [3, 3], budget = 6 -> [0, 1]
Constraints: 2 <= length <= 10^5

answerKey.pattern: One pass with a hash map from price to index (complement lookup)
keyPoints: For each index i compute need = budget - prices[i]
If need is already in the map, return [map[need], i]
Otherwise store prices[i] -> i
Checking before inserting prevents using the same ticket twice
edgeCases: Two equal prices, e.g. [3, 3] with budget 6
Must not pair a ticket with itself
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Nested loops over all pairs: O(n^2)
Sort with original indices kept, then two pointers: O(n log n)

title: Palindrome Name
statement:
Given a string, return true if it reads the same forwards and backwards after ignoring every character that is not a letter or digit and ignoring upper/lower case.

Example: "Ana-na" -> true
Example: "Rac e, car!" -> true
Example: "abc" -> false
Constraints: 0 <= length <= 2 * 10^5

answerKey.pattern: Two pointers moving inward from both ends
keyPoints: left = 0, right = last index
Skip characters that are not letters or digits on each side
Compare characters case-insensitively; if different return false
Move both pointers inward until they meet, then return true
edgeCases: String with only symbols returns true
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Build a cleaned lowercase copy and compare it with its reverse: O(n) time but O(n) extra space

title: Sorted Pair Target
statement:
Given an array of integers sorted in ascending order and a target, return the indices [i, j] (i < j) of two numbers that add up to the target. If no pair exists, return [-1, -1]. Use O(1) extra space.

Example: nums = [-4, 1, 3, 8, 11], target = 9 -> [1, 3]
Example: nums = [1, 2, 4], target = 10 -> [-1, -1]
Constraints: 2 <= length <= 10^5

answerKey.pattern: Two pointers at opposite ends, using the sorted order
keyPoints: left = 0, right = last index
If nums[left] + nums[right] == target return [left, right]
If the sum is smaller, move left forward (increase the sum)
If the sum is larger, move right backward (decrease the sum)
If the pointers meet, return [-1, -1]
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Hash map complement lookup: O(n) time but O(n) space, ignores the sorted order and the O(1) space requirement
